Voat doesn't currently have a AAAA record, so most users are probably using legacy IP to connect. You however can connect to Voat over IPv6 through cloudflare, and everything does appear to work fine.

Look up what IPv4 address you get back from cloudflare dns when resolving voat.co:

$ dig +short a voat.co
108.162.202.136
108.162.201.136

I've tested a few places geographically in the US and get those IPs back, but YMMV. Pick one and convert it into hex, so for 108.162.202.136:

$ printf '%x%x:%x%x' 108 162 202 136
6ca2:ca88

This becomes the low 32 bits of the address: 2400:cb00:2048:1::6ca2:ca88

You can add a local entry in your hosts file and the local resolver will use that for connecting to the site:

2400:cb00:2048:1::6ca2:ca88 voat.co

A word of warning, if you do this and voat changes how they're doing hosting / CDN-ing it could break for you until removing the hosts entry.

The problem is the order in which you declare things. Note that you should overwrite anything you have below the "Base CSS" section provided by Scribble, and you shouldn't really add multiple declarations to the same element; doing this can cause the browser to freak out, because it can't understand what you're trying to say (try having two friends shouting different things to you at the same time, it can get maddening). To solve this, I recommend simply merging all instances of "#header {" that you can find below the "Base CSS." After doing that, remember that "background-image" only takes one parameter: the url of the image. So "background-image: url(https://i.imgur.com/OHvun8p.png) no-repeat scroll center top;" simply won't work for a CSS rule. Instead, remove the "-image" part of that, and it suddenly becomes a multi-parameter declaration. The correct CSS should be:

#header {
 background: url(https://i.imgur.com/OHvun8p.png) no-repeat scroll center top;
}

Again, you should take every attempt to merge your CSS selectors, so you don't have a million of them. Remember that the bottom-most declaration is what gets carried out, unless there's one that says "!important" at the end of it. So, if you have the following:

#header {
 background: red;
 background: blue !important;
 background: green;
}

The background will be blue. If you remove that line of CSS, the background would be green. It is, in this example, completely safe to remove the "background: red" declaration. It's also safe to remove the "background: green" declaration if you decide to leave the blue one in there. You only ever need one rule per element.

I know, I know, giant wall of text, I'm sorry, but this is what it all boils down to: if you feel like learning, merge the rules so that each element (i.e. anything that comes before the "{" bracket). If you aren't comfortable with CSS, and you really don't want to learn it, then just keep adding to the bottom of it (note that this will eventually affect performance, and maintaining your code will become a nightmare, but if you never want to update Scribble, or anything else, then this may be the easiest and fastest option).
